# CVE to ASH test index

Publicly disclosed CVEs that the harness source cites, and the tests that exercise each one's vulnerability class. Each page has the vulnerability facts from primary sources, the test's own source lines, the command to run it, and what each verdict means.

A test here checks a vulnerability class against a target you are authorised to test. It is not a vendor exploit and a result does not establish that a deployment is or is not affected.

## Tests cited beside a documented CVE but not documented for it

| CVE | Test | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-2275 | CREW-002 | A harness self-test. Its own verdict text says it "Says nothing about the target." |
| CVE-2026-2275 | CREW-003 | Asks the agent to disclose its allow_code_execution setting. That observes configuration disclosure, not the sandbox-fallback behaviour the CVE describes. |
| CVE-2026-2286 | CREW-008 | Its verdict is computed only from the harness's own URL checker. Target responses are sent but cannot change the result, so it says nothing about the target. |

## How this list is kept honest

The CVEs and their test pairings are derived from `protocol_tests/`, not written by hand. `python scripts/generate_cve_pages.py --check`, run by `testing/test_cve_pages_are_current.py`, fails when the source cites a CVE the mapping does not account for, when a test paired with a CVE in source is neither documented nor withheld with a reason, when a test ID does not exist or is missing from [HARNESS_TEST_CATALOG.md](../../HARNESS_TEST_CATALOG.md), when a quoted source line is not verbatim at the pinned revision, or when these pages differ from regenerated output.

Vulnerability facts cannot be derived from this repository. They were retrieved from the sources named on each page and are re-retrieved, not edited, when updated.
